Hi there, Pizzagate truthers (I dunno... what are we calling ourselves?). I'm making this post primarily to gather my thoughts and see if there's a worthwhile thread I could be investigating, or if possibly these stories connect with anything anyone else might be aware of.

I was born in the mid 1980's, in a town called Texarkana, Texas, which is right on the state line separating Texas and Arkansas. Across the state line is the sister city, Texarkana, Arkansas.

Anecdote #1

My grandmother was a social worker for Arkansas child protective services, and every year that Bill Clinton was the governor of Arkansas, the budget for CPS would be drastically slashed, which in turn lead to reductions in the number of staff. My grandmother left her position because the workload had become so demanding that she could no longer provide adequate supervision of the children for whom she was the case worker.

She had 50 children to look after, and the state required that each child be visited once a week, and due to the budget reductions the kids any given case worker would need to see were placed all over the state.

As you may imagine, driving out, inspecting the living situation, talking with the child and care givers, and being able to responsibly determine whether the child was safe, healthy, and happy was not possible with such a workload. She left and went on to get her Master's in Social Work, and taught at a university for a few years before passing away in 2003. She kept a bunch of scrap books that had pictures and mementos of every one of the kids in her care; she was very dedicated and caring.

There are tons of flaws in the CPS/ Foster care services, and obviously I'm biased, but I know she was one of the good ones.

I cannot help but wonder if the child protective services were intentionally eroded, and if caring and intelligent people such as my grandmother were intentionally driven out. I see a mirror of this strategy going on in the education arena these days- the friends of mine that are/ were teachers seem to be experiencing the exact same squeeze in budgets and ridiculous increase in work load, and it seems that only the most sycophantic, orthodoxy-endorsing people can remain or get promoted in these kinds of conditions.

Anecdote #2:

My father and a friend of his were out camping near Mena, Arkansas, and had gotten a bit lost. It was night time. They were following a river to get back to civilization, when they saw a plane land in the middle of nowhere (on an airstrip... in the middle of nowhere). As soon as the plane landed, a boat in the river (that neither guy had noticed until just then) turned on its lights and sped off toward where the plane had landed. My dad and his buddy turned around and noped the fuck out of there, because there'd always been rumors about what went on under the Clintons, and no good Texan would ever permit himself the indecency of dying in Arkansas.

I'm well aware that the Mena, Arkansas thing has been on the record with us "conspiracy types" for a while, but it still seems important to note here.

Anecdote #3

When my mother went into labor with me, she was strapped to a table "like an animal" (her words) and wasn't allowed to hold me for like 4 hours. This was at a hospital in Bowie county, Texas. During those 4 hours, her father-in-law repeated gossip that he'd heard about nurses kidnapping babies, and/ or replacing white babies with mexican babies. To be fair, my grandfather was a) nuts and b) a douchebag, who disliked my mother.

This sent her into a panic, and her first instances of finally holding me were fear and questioning, trying to figure out if I was really hers (I look way too much like my dad to have been 'replaced,' but it's one of those stories that always comes up whenever we reminisce about my legendary asshole grandfather).

Incidentally, I would have been born on the Arkansas side of Texarkana, except for a law passed by Governor Clinton, which required that any hospital with a maternity ward also perform abortions. This caused all of the Catholic-run hospitals to get rid of their maternity wards (because obviously they're not going to perform abortions), and my mom being a good Catholic wanted to go to one of their hospitals. My parents like to joke that's the one good thing the Clintons ever did, because otherwise I would have been born in Arkansas (a word always spoken with a 'yuck' afterwards).

Americans on this forum will understand how religious and Conservative the American South is, and Arkansas is extremely Bible Belt-y.
